i.norm: When a header name is declared more than once, its mapping resolves to the last column index that bears that name. Here the header is declared twice (so the duplicate name maps to index 1), but the parsed input has only a single column (index 0). Because the mapped index 1 falls outside the record's one value, {@link CSVRecord#isSet(String)} reports that the column is not set.
Declare the same header name twice; the duplicate maps to the higher index (1).
The input contains a single column, so the record holds exactly one value (index 0).
